title: Twelve years as a staff musician at NBC and CBS
summary: He lists Hawaii Five-O, Danny Kaye, Carol Burnett and Flip Wilson shows, and says he refused to be bogged down in studio work.

story.theme_name: Radio and television work: staff jobs, shows and broadcasts
story.community_name: Working radio and television: network shows, studio staffs, talk-show bands

blocks.x: Oh, after that, let's see... I have to get a list of all the shows that I was involved in then. What's her name, Jo Diamond? You know you were in and out of the studios so much, it's hard to remember all the names. The things that stick in my mind most are later, like Hawaii Five-O, and then I went on staff at NBC and I did Let's Make A Deal or something like that. I was just on call for whatever they did. Later... I guess I'm getting ahead of myself, but it's okay. Later The Danny Kaye Show; I did that for four years at CBS. Following that, I spent four years doing the Carol Burnett Show, and mixed in between that, The Jonathan Winters Show and the Art Linkletter Show and then The Flip Wilson Show came along, and I left Carol Burnett to go with that. So I actually spent twelve years being a staff musician, too, which gave me a lot of freedom to do other things.
So what kinds of things did you do? Because some people who get staff positions like that get bogged down in studio work, and don't get out and do the other things.

Well, I refused to get bogged down. I managed to do record dates still, and... You know, I'd sandwich them in between the times I had to be on the studio, at the studio. Almost at the same time I did a thing that's just come back on, Rich Little is the host -- You Asked For It. I did that. Greg McRitchie(?) was the conductor, and I did that for about I guess three years. Meanwhile I was doing things with Nelson Riddle and Billy May, and even I did a lot of stuff with Lawrence Welk, a lot of polka albums playing tuba.
Well, a lot of good musicians have worked with Lawrence Welk.
Well, after he insisted on making an album with Johnny Hodges, I knew he had to be all right.
